evals.name: gap-with-deprecation-drift-corrected-toward-upstream
evals.prompt: recheck against upstream — our CI config still passes the build flag the way we set it up a year ago. It works, so we've never touched it.
evals.expected_output: Re-anchors the discipline that 'it works / it's already set up this way' is not evidence of current conformance, fetches the CURRENT official upstream docs for that surface, diffs the repo state against them, and classifies a docs-say-X-we-do-Y difference with no recorded rationale as a Gap — calling out any renamed flag, changed default, or deprecation as drift even though the old form still functions, then correcting toward upstream.
expectations: Rejects 'it works / already configured' as proof of conformance
Fetches current official upstream docs for the surface rather than relying on recall or an in-repo summary
Classifies the difference as a Gap and flags deprecation/version drift even when the old form still functions

evals.name: deliberate-divergence-rechecked-not-reverted
evals.prompt: recheck against upstream — we pin this dependency to an old version on purpose; there's an ADR explaining the incompatibility that forced it.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes the recorded rationale makes this a Deliberate divergence, so it does NOT correct it toward upstream. Instead it re-checks whether the rationale STILL holds against the current docs — whether upstream has since shipped a fix that obsoletes the pin — reporting clean if the rationale stands and flagging it only if the docs have overtaken it.
expectations: Classifies it as a deliberate divergence because a rationale is recorded, and does not revert it
Re-checks whether the recorded rationale still holds against current upstream rather than trusting it as permanent
Reports clean if the rationale stands; flags it only if upstream has obsoleted the workaround

evals.name: undocumented-divergence-routes-to-human-and-adr
evals.prompt: recheck against upstream — our setup does something different from the official quickstart, and I can't find any note saying why.
evals.expected_output: Classifies a state that looks intentional but has no recorded rationale as an Undocumented divergence whose resolution is the human's call — it does not silently pick a side. It states both options (adopt the docs' way, or keep the divergence and record its rationale) and routes the resolution to the repo's ADR/docs convention read from the consuming project's own context.
expectations: Classifies it as an undocumented divergence needing the human's decision rather than auto-correcting
States both resolution options (adopt upstream, or keep and document the rationale)
Routes resolution to the repo's ADR/docs convention rather than hardcoding a path

evals.name: honest-skip-list-not-false-clean
evals.prompt: recheck against upstream — verify our whole integration matches the vendor docs. (There are several surfaces; you were only able to fetch the docs for one of them this session.)
evals.expected_output: Reports honestly on what was compared versus what was skipped: it does not report the surfaces it could not fetch as 'clean'. Unverified conformance is stated as unaudited, with an explicit skip list, treating firing the skill as a re-anchor rather than an accusation.
expectations: Does not report un-compared surfaces as passing/clean
States an explicit list of what was compared versus skipped
Treats unverified conformance as unaudited rather than as a green result

evals.name: fan-out-doc-by-doc-over-the-subsystem
evals.prompt: /discipline:recheck-against-upstream fan-out — our whole payments integration leans on a dozen of the vendor's API surfaces and config blocks, and none of it has been checked against the docs in months.
evals.expected_output: Takes the fan-out tier. Enumerates every upstream-dependent surface in the subsystem rather than spot-checking one, dispatches fresh-context (blind) subagents to fetch the CURRENT official upstream docs for each surface and classify its divergence per the gap/deliberate/undocumented taxonomy, then merges the returns into an inline divergence ledger keyed by surface with the resolving source.
expectations: Takes /discipline:recheck-against-upstream's own fan-out tier on the `fan-out` argument (reading its reference/fan-out-tier.md), with no hand-off to a separate skill
Enumerates all upstream-dependent surfaces rather than checking one
Fans out fresh-context subagents that fetch current upstream docs per surface, not recall
Reports an inline divergence ledger keyed by surface, category, and resolving source

evals.name: fan-out-throttles-and-checkpoints-for-crash-safety
evals.prompt: Recheck the whole framework config against upstream — this is a big framework with dozens of config surfaces to compare.
evals.expected_output: Takes the fan-out tier. Throttles the dispatch into bounded waves with a concurrency cap rather than firing one agent per surface at once, notes the burst-overload (529) risk, retries only a failed surface once (marking a second failure unverifiable), and checkpoints the partial ledger to a durable topic-memory slice mid-run when one exists — proceeding without it when the session has no durable store rather than asserting a persistence surface.
expectations: Routes the whole-framework request to /discipline:recheck-against-upstream's own fan-out tier with no argument, rather than the inline single-surface recheck
Throttles into bounded waves with a concurrency cap and notes the 529 burst-overload risk
Retries only the failed subset once and marks a second failure unverifiable rather than blind-re-running
Checkpoints the partial ledger mid-run only when a durable slice exists, degrading gracefully when absent

evals.name: fan-out-offers-work-items-routing-and-degrades
evals.prompt: /discipline:recheck-against-upstream fan-out — audit the framework against upstream and help me turn what you find into trackable work.
evals.expected_output: After the fan-out, OFFERS to route category-1 (gap) and category-3 (undocumented) findings into tracked work items when a work-item capability is installed, degrading to a prose offer (a listed set of would-be items) when none is present. Category-2 (deliberate, still-valid) findings are report-only and are not routed unless the current docs have obsoleted them.
expectations: Takes /discipline:recheck-against-upstream's own fan-out tier on the `fan-out` argument before offering any routing
Offers to route gap and undocumented findings to a work-item capability when installed
Degrades to a prose offer when no work-item capability is present rather than assuming a tracker
Keeps still-valid deliberate divergences report-only rather than routing them

evals.name: single-surface-stays-inline
evals.prompt: /discipline:recheck-against-upstream — I just changed one setting in one config file; check it against the docs.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes that a single surface does not justify the subagent cost of a fan-out and runs the inline recheck instead of spinning up a broad verification pass over one surface.
expectations: Recognizes a single surface does not justify the fan-out's subagent cost
Runs the inline recheck rather than the fan-out tier
Does not manufacture a broad fan-out where an inline recheck suffices
Dispatches no subagent: the transcript shows no Agent call

evals.name: batched-fork-run-never-takes-fan-out-tier
evals.prompt: You are an audit-only fork dispatched by /discipline:sweep-all. Load /discipline:recheck-against-upstream, run re-anchor and self-audit only, make no writes, and return a findings ledger. (This session reworked a whole framework's configuration across dozens of upstream-dependent surfaces.)
evals.expected_output: Runs the inline recheck only, despite the whole-framework scope: a batched or forked run never takes the fan-out tier and dispatches no subagents. Its ledger names the surfaces it compared and those it skipped, and adds an entry recommending a direct /discipline:recheck-against-upstream fan-out run, rather than fanning out from inside the fork.
expectations: Does not dispatch any subagent or start the fan-out tier from inside the batched fork
Runs the inline re-anchor and self-audit and returns a findings ledger without writing, with an explicit compared-versus-skipped list
Recommends a direct /discipline:recheck-against-upstream fan-out run where the fan-out would fit
